findings.title: Negative-offset path in OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes on Django querysets
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and the cursor offset is negative, the code does `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` with a negative `start_offset`. Django's QuerySet explicitly disallows negative slicing (`Negative indexing is not supported` AssertionError), so instead of 'the ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' as the comment claims, any request that exercises this path returns a 500. Since cursor offsets are parsed from the client-supplied cursor string (`Cursor.from_string` accepts negative integers), a superuser on the audit log endpoint can trigger this with a crafted cursor. The feature is both broken and untested.

findings.title: organization_context.member may be None, causing AttributeError
findings.body: `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated on every audit log request, but `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is optional (None when the request is authorized via an org auth token/integration rather than a user membership). In that case this raises AttributeError and the endpoint 500s for a class of previously working requests. The superuser check should short-circuit safely and the member access needs a None guard.

findings.title: Redirect-follow loop limit silently reduced from 10000 to 1000
findings.body: The loop that follows span-id redirects was changed from 10000 to 1000 iterations. Segment trees deeper than 1000 redirects will now stop resolving early, so a span is attached to an intermediate set instead of the true root set, splitting one segment into multiple flushed segments (and leaving stale redirect entries). The previous code's comment explicitly warned about this failure mode at 10k; lowering the bound makes silent mis-grouping 10x more likely with no compensating metric or error when the limit is hit.

findings.title: max_segment_spans guard removed while Lua cap is hardcoded and inconsistent
findings.body: The `_load_segment_data` span-count safety check (`max_segment_spans`) was deleted and replaced by a hardcoded `if span_count > 1000 then zpopmin` in add-buffer.lua. Two problems: (1) the configurable `max_segment_spans=1001` constructor parameter is now dead code and no longer enforced anywhere; (2) eviction only happens inside the Lua script, so spans inserted via the initial `zadd` pipeline in `process_spans` (which runs before the script per batch) or races between consumers can still grow a set beyond the cap and will now be flushed unbounded, since the load-time check that previously dropped oversized segments is gone. Oversized segments can again produce multi-thousand-span Kafka messages.

findings.title: zpopmin evicts earliest-ending spans, biasing segment contents
findings.body: The eviction uses `zpopmin`, which removes the spans with the lowest score (earliest `end_timestamp_precise`). For a segment that exceeds 1000 spans this silently drops the oldest spans rather than the newest, which is the opposite of what one would typically want (keeping the root/earliest spans preserves segment structure), and dropped spans vanish with no metric or log, making the loss invisible in production.
